RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel on its own proves nothing. It's common in broadcasting management and is better understood as a governance weakness than as evidence about your case. Many employers' own guidance recommends mixed panels, so it's legitimate to note — but as context, not as your central claim.

Your stronger ground is the unanswered request for written reasons after two weeks, plus the gap between fifteen years' experience and eight. "Strong experience of digital media" is a plausible lawful rationale; you can't assess it until you see how the criteria were weighted and whether they were set before or after shortlisting.

So: raise the failure to respond now, request the scoring, and keep panel composition in reserve.
